title: Layoff Early-Warning for Credit Unions
one_liner: Turns public WARN notices and layoff signals into member-level outreach lists, so lenders can offer hardship plans about 60 days before payments are missed.
customer: Credit unions (roughly 4,400 in the US), community banks, mortgage servicers and auto lenders pay $1.5-6k a month, often via credit-union service organisations.
problem: White-collar layoffs are lumpy and local (information-sector employment fell 23k in one Aug 2026 month, Amazon cut ~16,000 corporate roles). Lenders learn about them from missed payments, when charge-off risk is already high and members are hardest to help. Hardship programs exist but outreach comes too late.
solution: Ingest state WARN databases, news and layoff trackers. Match employers to the lender's book using payroll ACH descriptors on member accounts. Rank members by exposure, then supply compliant outreach scripts, pre-approved skip-a-pay or modification offers, and uplift measurement.
why_now: Layoffs are steady and concentrated in higher-balance, AI-exposed white-collar borrowers. Payroll descriptors and open-banking data make the join easy. Small lenders have no data teams, and the low-hire market makes re-employment slow (7-13 months in practitioner reports).
revenue_model: SaaS at $1.5-6k a month per institution, or a performance fee on avoided delinquencies.
non_obvious_insight: The layoffs are public. The scarce piece is the join to the lender's book via payroll descriptors. Employees of a laid-off employer often bank at the same local credit union, so the risk is concentrated, and the ROI is stated in avoided charge-offs rather than charity.
first_30_days: Normalise 50 state WARN sources. Backtest with a friendly credit union on two past layoff events to show missed payments 45-90 days later. Get two credit-union service organisations to run a paid $1k-a-month pilot.

title: Dead Capital: Succession Kits for Diaspora Families
one_liner: A flat-fee, advocate-supervised 'estate file' service that gets a dead parent's or grandfather's land, shares and dormant accounts legally transferred, sold to the adult children who pay from Nairobi, Dallas or Dubai.
customer: Salaried urban and diaspora Kenyans aged 30-55 whose rural parents or grandparents died (or are old) with land still registered in a dead person's name. They pay from abroad or from the city. A secondary B2B payer is any SACCO, coop or bank that needs cleared successions before it releases deposits or lends against land.
problem: Most rural family land is still titled to a dead grandfather or father because nobody completed succession. The process needs a chief's letter, a death certificate, consents from every heir, gazettement, a wait before confirmation of grant, and then transmission at the land registry, which is often 1-3 years and many trips. Until it is done the land cannot be leased, mortgaged, subdivided or cleanly sold, siblings fight, and the deceased's SACCO deposits, coop shares, insurance and pension sit unclaimed. The real blocker is coordinating 8 to 20 relatives to sign, not the court.
solution: Wedge product is a 'Family Estate Map' for roughly KES 15-25k (pricing to be tested). The child sends photos of the title, IDs, death certificate and old share certificates over WhatsApp. An LLM pipeline extracts names and parcel numbers, handles the multiple-name and spelling-variant problem in Kenyan naming, builds the family tree and likely heirs, and lists the consents needed. It runs official land searches and asset-discovery letters to SACCOs, coops, insurers and the Unclaimed Financial Assets Authority, then outputs a court-ready bundle of forms and affidavits. A home-county field agent collects the chief's letter and relatives' signatures or thumbprints, with video proof of consent. Partner advocates then file and shepherd the case at their own scale fees. Later upsells are surveyor subdivision and lease or loan readiness.
why_now: The generation that took up land in the 1960s-80s through settlement schemes and land-buying companies is dying now, so the succession backlog is peaking. Diaspora remittances are near record levels (roughly US$5bn a year), and families increasingly ask 'sort out the land' rather than 'build a house'. Digitised land records (Ardhisasa) and court e-filing reduce physical running, though their current coverage needs checking. LLMs can now read messy scanned title and ID documents and draft forms in English while chatting with clients in Swahili. I could not run live searches, so verify current UFAA agent rules, court e-filing scope for successions, and fee schedules before building.
revenue_model: Flat fee per estate file, paid by M-Pesa or card from abroad. Advocate fees are billed by the advocates themselves, so the company sells software and case management and does not split fees with non-lawyers. Asset discovery is a flat add-on fee, not a percentage cut of UFAA payouts, because UFAA discourages middlemen taking a share. B2B revenue is per cleaned member estate from SACCOs and coops. Later there is referral income from surveyors and land-backed lenders once titles are clean.
non_obvious_insight: Rural Kenya's biggest pool of unused collateral is land trapped in the name of the dead. The bottleneck is family coordination and evidence gathering, so the product is a coordination workflow sold to the sibling who has money and guilt, not a land registry or a lawyer marketplace. VCs looking at land-tech miss that the payer is the diaspora child, not the farmer.
first_30_days: Pick one county (for example Murang'a or Kakamega) and recruit two advocates who already do succession work. Build intake on WhatsApp Business, Airtable and an LLM extraction script. Sell 10 files at a pilot discount through your own family network, church and alumni groups, and diaspora WhatsApp and Facebook groups such as Kenyans in Texas or the UK. Publish a free 'Is your family land still in a dead man's name?' checker as lead-gen. Track days from intake to gazettement as the core metric.

title: Condition-Based Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning Sensors
one_liner: Duct-mounted grease-film sensor pods, sold through hood-cleaning contractors, that predict when a restaurant's exhaust system actually needs cleaning and prove the cleaning was done.
customer: Independent commercial kitchen exhaust cleaning contractors (5-50 technicians) as the channel and first payer. End users are restaurants, hotels, hospital and campus kitchens, and ghost-kitchen operators, with commercial property insurers as a downstream discount payer.
problem: NFPA 96 sets calendar cleaning intervals from monthly to annual by cooking type, but real grease buildup varies enormously by menu (wok, charbroil and fryer kitchens versus sandwich shops). The result is over-cleaning in some places and dangerous under-cleaning in others. Restaurants can't see inside their ducts, so they can't verify that hard-to-reach plenum and duct runs were really cleaned. Grease is a leading cause of restaurant fires and property insurers increasingly want documentation.
solution: A retrofit pod at the hood plenum and an access panel, with temperature, airflow or differential-pressure, fan-current and a capacitive grease-film sensor. It uses BLE or LoRa to a small gateway. An edge model outputs 'days to cleaning threshold' and schedules the contractor. After each cleaning the pod records a post-clean baseline, which becomes tamper-evident proof for the restaurant, the fire inspector and the insurer. Start with sensors outside the duct interior (plenum, access panel) to avoid grease and heat survivability problems.
why_now: Cheap MEMS and capacitive sensing plus LoRa/BLE make a sub-USD-100 pod feasible. Documentation expectations in recent NFPA 96 editions and commercial property insurance hardening push restaurants toward provable maintenance. Contractors face thin margins and want stickier recurring contracts.
revenue_model: Hardware at USD 180-350 per hood, or leased. Subscription of USD 25-45 per month per hood, with a 30% revenue share to the contractor who resells and installs. Pilot insurer premium-credit program. Contractor-side scheduling and route-optimization software as an upsell.
non_obvious_insight: The real buyer is the cleaner, not the restaurant. Monitoring turns a commodity route-calendar service into a data-backed recurring contract and cuts wasted truck rolls. The most valuable reading is not the continuous alert but the after-clean baseline, because the actual pain is 'did they really clean the duct?' That is a trust problem no one solves today.
first_30_days: Prototype a pod from off-the-shelf sensors. Recruit three cleaning contractors through the International Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning Association network and offer free pods on 10 hoods each. Log grease-accumulation curves by cuisine type for 60-90 days. Show the contractors their own before/after evidence, then sell the first paid subscriptions with revenue share.

title: AI-Use Attestation to Keep SMB Liability Cover
one_liner: As liability policies exclude generative AI, small firms need underwriter-ready proof of AI controls to win affirmative cover, and independent agencies need a renewal ritual that keeps them relevant.
customer: Independent insurance agencies (about 37k remain) that place GL and E&O for law firms, accountants, marketing agencies, clinics and contractors, plus those SMB clients.
problem: ISO's gen-AI exclusion is already on thousands of CGL policies (Insurance Business, 2026-09-16). AI-specialist insurers target tech firms, not a dental practice using an AI receptionist. Agencies can't advise and carriers haven't said what evidence they'd accept, so clients discover the gap at claim time.
solution: A lightweight AI Use Register: discover which AI tools staff use (SSO and browser discovery), apply policy templates and human-review logging, and output a standardized attestation that a panel of MGAs and carriers agree to accept for endorsements or premium credits. Agencies white-label it into their renewal workflow.
why_now: Exclusions are spreading now, independent agencies are shrinking (39k in 2024 to 37k in 2026, Insurance Journal) yet still sell 95% of commercial insurance through humans, and insurtech's dollars (99.1% of Q2 funding is AI-centric) go to back-office tools, not SMB risk evidence.
revenue_model: $49-$149 per month per SMB, billed via the agency or the client, plus MGA per-policy referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: Carriers don't yet know what evidence they want, so whoever standardizes the artifact defines it, as cyber questionnaires and scans did for Coalition and At-Bay. Agencies get a reason to call every client at renewal.
first_30_days: Interview five underwriters on what evidence they'd accept. Ship a spreadsheet-and-form v0 of the register. Sell it to 10 agencies through state agent-association chapters and get 30 SMBs onto paid plans.

title: Remote Load Calcs That Avoid Panel Upgrades
one_liner: A photo-and-utility-bill service that proves an existing electrical panel can take a heat pump or EV charger, with load-management devices when it cannot.
customer: HVAC and heat-pump contractors, EV-charger installers and solar-plus-storage installers without in-house electricians. Later: state and utility electrification programs.
problem: Data centers are absorbing electricians (nearly a third of the shortage; Texas builders report electrical delays of up to 2 months). Residential electrician time becomes the scarcest input, so panel upgrades stall every electrification job. HVAC contractors selling heat pumps are blocked by work they do not do and cannot schedule. The HVAC rebound expected in 2027 will make it worse.
solution: Installer uploads a photo of the panel label plus 12 months of utility data. The service returns a permit-ready load calculation under the existing-load method, stamped by a remote licensed engineer or electrician. It recommends the cheapest path: no upgrade, a load-management or circuit-pausing device allowed by recent NEC editions, or a smart panel, with the material list for the installer's quote.
why_now: Electrician scarcity from data-center overtime ($130-170K, vendor stat), 2027 HVAC rebound with A2L certification adding friction, and a 110K technician shortage. Load-management devices and energy-management provisions are now commercially available and code-recognized in many places.
revenue_model: $79-149 per calculation billed to installers. Annual contracts with programs. Referral margin from load-management device makers.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck for electrification is neither the heat pump nor the HVAC tech, it is the panel and the electrician-days it consumes. Avoiding electrician hours is worth more than adding them, and the existing truck-roll panel check can be done as a $99 desk job by one remote engineer serving many installers.
first_30_days: Sign 20 HVAC contractors in one state. Contract a licensed PE or master electrician for templates and stamps. Deliver 50 calculations by hand. Measure the percentage that avoided an upgrade.

title: Cash-Flow Lifeline for K-12 Service Vendors
one_liner: Same-week invoice funding for small vendors who serve schools (after-school, tutoring, therapy, van companies), priced using each district's known payment calendar, with a service-continuity guarantee for principals.
customer: Small K-12 vendors paying a financing fee: after-school providers, contract speech, occupational and counseling practices, tutoring companies, small van and transportation contractors, and arts and PE providers. Principals are the sponsor and the free channel.
problem: Districts pay invoices 60 to 120 days late, and federal-grant reimbursements (21st Century, Title programs) lag further. Small vendors run out of cash and vanish in October, mid-year, leaving kids without services. Principals cannot legally pay faster and get blamed when the therapist stops coming. Generic factoring companies price district risk like a private customer or refuse it.
solution: Fund invoices within 48 hours at 90 percent advance. Verification is a text or QR 'services delivered' confirmation from the principal, which is the step district accounts payable needs anyway. Price risk using each district's board-approval calendar, warrant runs and reimbursement cycles, which we assemble from public board minutes. Add a continuity guarantee: if a funded vendor fails, a pre-vetted bench vendor steps in. Districts get a simple notice-of-assignment form to sign.
why_now: The July 2025 withholding of roughly $6.8B in federal education funds, released weeks later, showed how fragile the timing is. Post-ESSER budgets are tight, and small-business credit is harder for vendors with slow government customers. LLMs can now read board packets, purchase orders and approval calendars at scale to predict pay dates.
revenue_model: Fee of about 1.5 to 3 percent per invoice per 30 days advanced, plus a vendor subscription ($99 per month) for the delivery-confirmation and invoicing workflow.
non_obvious_insight: District default risk is near zero. The risk is timing, and timing is predictable if you know how boards and warrant runs work. The principal's confirmation, not the bank, is the bottleneck, so whoever owns that step owns the data. Investors dismiss K-12 as slow and poor, but the payer is a taxing authority, which is the safest receivable there is.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 small vendors from principals' and coordinators' contact lists, starting with after-school and therapy contractors that have already had payment problems. Raise $150k to $300k of angel or warehouse capital and fund the first invoices at a flat fee. Build the district payment calendars in a spreadsheet from public minutes, which becomes the pricing model and the data moat.

title: Foreign-Ties Clearance Pack for SBIR Startups
one_liner: A fixed-price, agency-ready foreign-involvement and cyber-readiness dossier priced to fit inside the SBIR technical-assistance allowance, so the startup pays nothing out of pocket.
customer: SBIR/STTR Phase I and Phase II applicants and awardees (DoD, DOE, NSF, NIH, EPA). Secondary buyers are seed and VC funds with SBIR-heavy portfolios that need LP-level attestations for their companies.
problem: The Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act (S. 3971, signed April 13, 2026, extends SBIR/STTR through FY2031) makes agencies run risk-based due diligence on every applicant. The review covers foreign ownership and financial ties, foreign affiliations of key personnel, licensing deals and joint ventures, and links to the UFLPA, Chinese Military-Industrial Complex, Commerce Entity and Section 889 lists. It also covers cybersecurity practices, patent analysis and employee analysis. Applicants must file disclosures. A 4-person startup has no idea what an agency will find in its cap table (LPs behind the VC funds), co-inventors, or contractors. Agencies may notify of a denial only 'as appropriate', so a rejection may come with no explanation.
solution: A software-plus-analyst service that ingests the cap table, team list, patents and vendor list. It does look-through on investors (SEC Form ADV and Form D, GLEIF, OpenCorporates). It screens every name against the free BIS Consolidated Screening List and the UFLPA and CMIC lists. It checks co-inventor and employee affiliations (USPTO PatentsView, ORCID) and takes a NIST 800-171/SPRS cyber baseline. Output is a disclosure-ready packet, a red-flag remediation memo (for example 'restructure this side letter'), and a yearly re-screen. Sold as a vendor the awardee can pick for technical and business assistance (T&BA) money.
why_now: S. 3971 was signed April 13, 2026. The T&BA allowance was raised to $6,500 per Phase I and $50,000 per Phase II, and it now explicitly covers 'cybersecurity assistance' and 'screening for potential foreign involvement'. The lapse from October 2025 to April 2026 created a backlog: DOE alone opened about $147M of FY25 Phase II on July 22, 2026, and the FY26 Genesis Mission Phase I is open. Every awardee now faces the new diligence for the first time.
revenue_model: $2,500 to $6,500 flat per Phase I (fits under the $6,500 T&BA cap, so it is free to the founder). $15k to $50k per Phase II package. $1,200 per year for a re-screen subscription when the cap table changes. VC portfolio bundles at $500 to $1,000 per company.
non_obvious_insight: Congress created an earmarked wallet for exactly this service, and the buyer has zero price sensitivity because the money can't be spent on anything else. S. 3971 Section 7 amends Section 9(q) to allow T&BA funds for 'cybersecurity assistance' and 'screening for potential foreign involvement', up to $6,500 (Phase I) and $50,000 (Phase II) per project, and lets recipients choose their own vendors. Section 2 (new Section 9(vv)) lists the diligence factors agencies must assess (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3971enr/html/BILLS-119s3971enr.htm). DOE confirms the April 13, 2026 signing, extension through FY2031, new security due-diligence mandates, and the reopened Phase II money (https://www.energy.gov/technologycommercialization/doe-small-business-innovation-research-sbir-and-small-business). The hard part is not screening names but LP-level look-through on venture funds, which is opaque and which no compliance vendor packages for a 4-person startup. Caveat: I could not confirm which agencies have opened T&BA vendor lists yet, so check that first.
first_30_days: Week 1: build a free 'SBIR foreign-risk self-check' web tool on top of the BIS Consolidated Screening List API and the UFLPA list. Use it as the lead magnet. Weeks 1 to 2: pull the last 12 months of Phase I/II awardees from the public SBIR.gov awards data and email 300 founders quoting the exact statute language. Weeks 2 to 4: manually produce 5 free dossiers for design partners to learn where the LP look-through breaks. Ask each agency SBIR office (start with DOE OTC, NSF and Navy) how to be listed as a T&BA vendor. Close 5 paid packs at $2.5k to $6.5k.

title: Emeritus: Paying 80-Year-Old Tradespeople for Tacit Knowledge
one_liner: Recruit retired machinists, lineworkers, boiler operators and railroad and telephone technicians in their 70s-90s, pay them hourly to teach on camera, and sell the corpus to AI labs, robotics companies and industrial firms.
customer: Robotics and embodied-AI labs, LLM data buyers who have exhausted white-collar experts, and utilities and plants that run 1970s-era equipment.
problem: The last generation with hand skills and legacy-system judgment is disappearing. Companies try to capture knowledge from employees before retirement with KM software, but the deepest experts left years ago and can't be reached by enterprise tools. AI labs pay $75-200+/hr to lawyers and doctors through Mercor and Surge but have thin coverage of physical-process knowledge. Retirees are invisible to gig platforms.
solution: A field-producer model. Partner with union retiree clubs, trade associations and retiree chapters (IBEW, IAM, railroad retiree groups). Send a two-person crew with a phone rig and lav mics to sit with each retiree in their garage, shop or a plant visit. Run structured 'teach-back' sessions on failure modes, sounds, smells and shortcuts. Transcribe, segment and tag with AI. Pay the expert $60-120/hr plus a royalty share when the corpus is licensed. Sell curated, rights-cleared datasets and 'ask the old-timer' search seats to plants.
why_now: AI labs are spending heavily on expert data (Mercor reportedly pays contractors about $1.5M a day), and humanoid and robotics teams need process knowledge. About 40% of the manufacturing workforce is retirement-eligible within a decade, and utilities report up to half pension-eligible by 2027. Multimodal models can now ingest video and audio at scale.
revenue_model: Dataset licensing per hour of tagged, rights-cleared sessions ($500-2,000/hr). Enterprise capture projects ($30-150k). Per-seat search and Q&A licenses. Expert royalties are a cost of goods, which is also the recruiting pitch.
non_obvious_insight: The scarcest expert data isn't PhDs but the 82-year-old who can diagnose a turbine by sound. Retirees are also the only experts with no employer NDA or IP claim, so their data rights are cleaner and they can sign licenses directly. For the elder, it is paid, respected work and social contact, which is what tech never offers 80-year-olds.
first_30_days: Pick one niche (say retired tool-and-die makers or utility lineworkers) and recruit through three retiree-association newsletters. Pay 15 experts $100/hr for 2-hour sessions and produce about 30 hours. Have a lawyer draft consent and licensing contracts with cognitive-capacity safeguards and a family representative. Send samples to 3 robotics companies and 2 utilities.

title: Seasonal Staff Housing from Banned Rentals
one_liner: Master-lease flats stranded by short-term-rental bans and sublet them by the bed, with employer-guaranteed rent, to short-staffed hotels in the same destination.
customer: Hotels, resorts and restaurant groups with 50-400 seasonal staff in Palma, Ibiza, Barcelona coast and similar hotspots (start in the Balearics). Secondary customer: small owners whose licences are ending.
problem: Insiders frame STR bans as residents versus tourists, with owners as the losers. The overlooked fact is that banned owners have empty flats and fear 12-month tenancy law, while the hotel next door cannot hire because staff cannot find housing. Nobody sits in the middle to handle leases, furnishing, inspections and deposits.
solution: An asset-light intermediary signs 6-11 month leases with owners under a structure vetted by local counsel. The hotel guarantees the rent and places its own staff. We handle furnishing, house rules, inspections and optional payroll-deduction of rent, and charge per bed. The wedge is one Palma pilot with 3 hotels and about 30 flats.
why_now: Palma has a full ban, Barcelona bans all STRs in Nov 2028 after Spain's top court upheld it in Oct 2025, and Madrid restricts listings. Spain fined Airbnb $75M in Dec 2025, so the stranded supply is real. Spain still had about 97M visitors, so hotels are staffing to record demand.
revenue_model: A 12-18% management fee on rent, or a EUR 40-70 per bed per month spread, plus a placement fee from the hotel and a fee for guaranteeing rent to the owner.
non_obvious_insight: A ban strands supply as well as demand, and the best tenant for that supply is the employer of the people who service tourism. Employer-guaranteed rent is better credit than any nomad or mid-term tenant, which lets owners accept lower rents for zero vacancy risk.
first_30_days: Contact HR and operations heads at 15 hotels through the Mallorca hoteliers' federation and LinkedIn, and sign 3 letters of intent for 10-20 beds each. Recruit 30 owners through ex-STR property managers and owner groups. Pay a local lawyer EUR 3-5K for a lease template. Sign leases only after the hotel LOIs are in.

title: Trust Oracle for Rental Listings and Agents
one_liner: An API that answers whether a vacation rental exists, is legally registered and is controlled by the host, so payment firms, insurers and AI booking agents can refuse scams.
customer: Payment providers handling travel, travel insurers, villa-rental agencies and AI trip-agent developers, later consumers via a plug-in.
problem: AI-generated photos and cloned listings fuel rental fraud, and agents will soon book unattended. The EU short-term rental regulation requires registration numbers from May 2026, but there is no cross-border way to verify them and each registry differs. Bans (Barcelona 2028, Palma) will also see illegal listings delisted at the last minute, stranding guests.
solution: Aggregate public registries (Spain, Portugal, Italy, Greece, France, NYC and others), geocode the address and match it to satellite and street imagery, reverse-search photos and detect duplicates. Return a verified, unverified or unregistered verdict with evidence in under two seconds, as an API and an agent tool.
why_now: Registry numbers make 'is it legal' a lookup for the first time, agentic booking needs automated trust, and AI imagery has broken manual checks. Enforcement is rising (Spain's USD 75M fine on Airbnb).
revenue_model: USD 0.05-0.50 per check, USD 2-10K per month enterprise plans, and a share of insurer premiums saved.
non_obvious_insight: Registration numbers convert legality from opinion into data, and agents cannot get a bad feeling about a listing. Whoever builds the legality and fraud graph first becomes infrastructure for every automated booking flow.
first_30_days: Build for Spain, Italy and Portugal using public registers. Offer a free check widget to villa agencies, and backtest known scam cases to pitch two travel-insurer fraud teams.

title: L-Band Radar Watchdog for Small Levee Districts
one_liner: Turn free NISAR L-band radar into monthly, engineer-stamped settlement and seepage alerts for the small local districts that own most of America's levees.
customer: Reclamation, levee and drainage districts (California Delta and Central Valley, Iowa/Illinois/Missouri/Arkansas drainage districts) and owners of small high-hazard earthen dams and irrigation canals. Budgets are $50k to $2M a year, run by a board plus a part-time manager.
problem: Grass-covered earthen levees lose coherence in C-band InSAR (Sentinel-1), so cheap remote settlement monitoring never worked on them. Districts rely on annual walk-through inspections by volunteers or consultants. Failures are catastrophic, and grant, subvention and insurance paperwork demands documented condition history that most districts lack.
solution: A pipeline on NISAR L-band (about 10 m, 12-day repeat, which sees through vegetation) plus Sentinel-1 and soil-moisture change. It produces per-levee-mile maps of slumping, settlement and unusual wetness (seepage proxy). Alerts go to a partner licensed geotechnical engineer, who signs a one-page condition letter. The district attaches that letter to state levee-subvention and federal rehabilitation-program files, insurer renewals and board minutes. The dashboard is secondary; the stamped trigger is the product.
why_now: NASA/ISRO began releasing NISAR L-band data free through ASF DAAC on July 20, 2026 (acquisitions from June 17, 2026; full science record due by end of 2026). Tens of thousands of levee miles are locally owned, and nobody had L-band time series at this cadence before. Whoever starts the baseline now owns the longest history.
revenue_model: Subscription of $3k to $8k a year per district, tiered by levee miles. Add $1.5k to $4k per engineer-stamped event report. Later, portfolio-level data licences to flood insurers and reinsurers, and to state agencies that fund many districts.
non_obvious_insight: The radar data is free and commoditizing, so the data is not what the customer buys. They buy a defensible, professionally signed trigger that unlocks grant money, satisfies insurers and shifts liability. The moat is the engineer-of-record relationship, local ground truth and a baseline archive that starts accumulating today.
first_30_days: Process Sentinel-1, ALOS-2 and the first NISAR stacks over one Delta island or Iowa drainage district with a known past slump, to show a retrospective catch. Sign a geotech firm as engineer of record. Offer 5 districts a free baseline map and a $1.5k pilot, pitched at levee-district association and flood-board meetings. Aim for 2 paid pilots by day 30.

title: H-2A Housing-as-a-Service for Growers
one_liner: Lease pre-certified modular seasonal housing by the bed so growers can actually use H-2A visas.
customer: Specialty-crop growers and farm labor contractors in CA, WA, GA and the Southeast.
problem: Immigration enforcement removed at least 155,000 farm workers and H-2A is projected to grow toward 500k jobs, but employers must supply inspected housing, which is scarce and slow to build.
solution: A fleet of modular bunk units that pass DOL and OSHA housing inspection, delivered to farms or leased sites for the season, with paperwork and maintenance handled.
why_now: The October 2025 wage-rule change and enforcement-driven crew losses push growers to H-2A at scale, making beds the binding constraint.
revenue_model: Per-bed-month lease of roughly $X seasonal contracts with multi-year renewals.
non_obvious_insight: Visa wages get the headlines, but whoever owns compliant beds owns the labor channel. Housing is asset-backed, financeable and repeats every season.
first_30_days: Pre-sell 100 beds for the 2027 season to five growers with deposits, source used modular units, and get one prototype unit through a state housing inspection.

title: Blended-Beef Extender for Grinders and Schools
one_liner: Sell a fiber-and-protein extender that stretches ground beef 20-30% and adds fiber, instead of trying to replace beef.
customer: Regional ground-beef grinders, further processors, and school and institutional foodservice distributors.
problem: Retail beef hit a record $9.64/lb with the smallest herd in 75 years, and Mexican feeder cattle are halted. Plant-based meat failed as a replacement, so buyers have no cost-relief tool.
solution: A mushroom, legume and oat fiber-protein blend with a clean label, tested in 70/30 and 80/20 beef blends, sold by the ton with USDA-compliant blended-product labeling and recipe support.
why_now: Record beef prices, screwworm-driven supply risk, and GLP-1 users who want more protein and fiber per bite make a cheaper high-fiber blended patty newly attractive.
revenue_model: Ingredient sales per pound, co-development fees, and multi-year supply agreements with distributors.
non_obvious_insight: Plant-based meat lost as an identity swap but wins as a cost and fiber additive inside real beef, where the buyer never has to change what they say they are selling.
first_30_days: Contract a food-science lab to build three blends, send samples to about 10 regional grinders and two school-food distributors, and start FSIS labeling work.

title: Pre-Inspected Wildfire Books From Moratorium Zip Codes
one_liner: Turn California's public nonrenewal-moratorium ZIP lists into a supply of mitigation-verified risks, sold to carriers and MGAs who want good business and to commercial-residential owners who need it.
customer: Two payers. Admitted and E&S carriers or MGAs pay $75-150 per bound policy for a pre-inspected, standardized risk file. HOAs, apartment owners, senior-living operators and nonprofits pay $300-1,500 per building for verified defensible-space and hardening reports.
problem: California's wildfire nonrenewal moratoria last one year from the emergency declaration (up to 24 months for total losses), then the protection ends. More than 147,000 policyholders sit in 29 Gifford Fire ZIP codes, and over 64,000 in 22 Gann Fire ZIP codes. Since SB 547 took effect on 2026-01-01, commercial residential owners are covered for the first time, so they will face renewal shock too. Carriers lack standardized ground-truth mitigation evidence, and owners have no cheap way to produce it.
solution: A mitigation-verification package aligned to the state's Safer from Wildfires discount framework. It covers ember-resistant vents, Zone 0 clearance, roof class, and geotagged photo evidence with an inspector attestation. The result is a portable underwriting file. We start with commercial residential buildings, where one manager decision covers many units and the owners are reachable, and then sell the file to carriers as a pre-underwritten book.
why_now: The Gifford Fire moratorium (emergency declared 2025-12-23) expires around 2026-12-23, about 86 days from today. The Gann Fire moratorium began 2026-08-06. The FAIR Plan hit 696,562 policies and $768B of exposure in June 2026, up 157% and 250% since September 2022. Carriers have been restricting writing statewide, and the state has told them to give wildfire safety discounts.
revenue_model: Inspection fees from commercial-residential owners ($300-1,500 per building), plus per-bind fees or a basis-point share of premium from carriers and MGAs taking the verified files. Later upsell of reinspection subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: The moratorium notices are effectively a public, geocoded list of about 210,000 policyholders whose insurability will be decided by mitigation evidence within months. See https://www.insurance.ca.gov/0400-news/0100-press-releases/2025/release002-2026.cfm (Gifford: 147,000+ policyholders, 29 ZIPs, one year from 2025-12-23, up to 24 months for total loss, SB 547 extends to businesses, associations, affordable housing, senior facilities and nonprofits) and https://www.insurance.ca.gov/0400-news/0100-press-releases/2026/release027-2026.cfm (Gann: 64,000+, 22 ZIPs). FAIR Plan growth is at https://www.cfpnet.com/key-statistics-data/. Cotality found 2.5M US properties with $1.4T wildfire exposure (https://www.cotality.com/press-releases/over-2-5m-u-s-properties-face-wildfire-risk-with-1-4tn-exposed). I could not confirm carrier re-entry commitments in this session, so the carrier-side demand is a hypothesis to test with 3 MGAs before scaling. The wedge sells to reachable commercial-residential owners first, and the carrier data sale follows once the files exist.
first_30_days: Download the ZIP lists for Gifford and Gann and geocode commercial-residential buildings (HOAs, apartments, senior living) from county parcel and permit data. Train 2 inspectors on a one-page checklist based on the state discount framework. Cold-call 40 property managers in the Gifford ZIPs before 2026-12-23 and offer a discounted first inspection. Show 3 MGAs sample files and ask what fields they would pay for.

title: Zero-Retention Edge Enforcement for City Cameras
one_liner: Privacy-proof add-on analytics for existing plate readers and CCTV that keep only violation events and cryptographically delete everything else.
customer: Mid-size cities and towns in states that authorize automated enforcement (noise, illegal dumping, stop-arm, blocked bus lanes), starting with Connecticut, plus police departments under pressure over Flock-style data retention.
problem: Connecticut towns are bolting audio detectors onto existing plate readers for noise enforcement, while Ohio bills and public backlash attack camera surveillance. Cities want the revenue but fear becoming the next headline about bulk data retention.
solution: Edge box or firmware add-on that runs detection on-device and stores only the evidence clip for a confirmed violation. Everything else is deleted with signed deletion logs that auditors can verify. Sold as a rev-share enforcement program with a city-adoptable privacy ordinance template.
why_now: Connecticut's 2024 noise-camera law is live in West Haven, Wethersfield and East Hartford. Ohio bills show the Flock backlash is turning legislative. Cheap edge inference makes on-device analytics viable.
revenue_model: Per-citation or per-camera-month fee (for example 20-30% of net citation revenue, or $150-300 per camera per month), plus a one-time install fee.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders read the backlash as the end of sensor stacking. It is actually a moat for whoever makes data architecturally un-repurposable. Privacy becomes the procurement feature that survives a city council vote.
first_30_days: Pitch 5 Connecticut towns already running noise pilots to add a pilot with a retention-proof log. Build the demo on an off-the-shelf edge board with an existing LPR feed. Draft the ordinance template with a municipal attorney.

title: Public-Access TV Stations Become Media Notaries
one_liner: Convert struggling PEG community-media centers into witnessed-recording and signing hubs that cities pay to certify official meeting video and creators pay to prove a recording was performed live by a human in a real room.
customer: City and county clerks ($300-600/month for signed, canonical video of meetings, hearings and emergency briefings), PEG access centers (keep about 60% as delivery partners), and local musicians, podcasters and hyperlocal news creators ($45 per witnessed session or $15/month for verified-clip embeds). Later buyers are sync buyers and ad agencies.
problem: PEG centers (public, educational and government access TV) are funded by cable franchise fees that erode as cable subscriptions fall (prior knowledge), yet they own studios, gear, staff and a role recording local government. Meanwhile fully AI tracks passed 50% of Deezer uploads (July 2026), AI-cloned officials' clips circulate, platform human badges are free and per-artist (Spotify) or absent (YouTube will not demote labeled AI), and detectors are only probabilistic. Nobody sells 'this was made live, in this room, on this date, witnessed by a public institution'.
solution: A roughly $600 witness kit plus software: hardware-signed capture into C2PA manifests, staff-attested session logs with an ID check of performers, and raw timestamped multitrack takes. Cities get a canonical signed meeting archive and a public 'verify this clip' page. Local news creators embed verified clips, and artists attach a 'Recorded live at [Center], [date]' credential to releases and distributor metadata.
why_now: EU AI Act Article 50 marking and disclosure duties started applying 2026-08-02. C2PA 2.3 and TikTok's July 2026 steering-committee entry mean signed media can now travel across platforms. Platforms went from tolerating to policing AI in months (Bandcamp ban, Spotify AI Persona labels, TIDAL demonetization), and PEG funding pressure means centers need new revenue lines.
revenue_model: City subscriptions, per-session fees split with PEG centers, an annual software license to centers, and later per-clip verification fees from sync buyers.
non_obvious_insight: A credential is only as trustworthy as the institution behind it. Platforms cannot referee because they sell AI tools, and detectors give probabilities while a witness gives testimony. PEG centers are the only neutral, government-adjacent, physically distributed and already-recording institutions in most towns, and their core asset is exactly what provenance lacks: a place and a person willing to attest.
first_30_days: Contact the Alliance for Community Media state chapters and equip 3 PEG stations in one state. Sign one month of council meetings free, then demo a deepfaked council clip against the signed original to sell a $300/month city plan. Open 'Witnessed Live' studio hours to 20 local artists at $45.

title: Pay-Per-Win Appeals Desk for Nursing Homes
one_liner: A 24/7 appeal desk that turns every Medicare Advantage post-acute denial and coverage-termination notice into a filed appeal, paid only when the plan reverses.
customer: Independent and regional skilled nursing operators (3-30 facilities), plus home health agencies and inpatient rehab units that live on Medicare Advantage authorizations and have no appeals staff.
problem: A federal OIG review reported by Healthcare Dive found MA plans denied about 12% of SNF requests, about 67% of LTACH and over 50% of inpatient-rehab requests. SNFs appealed fewer than 20% of denials, yet 95% of those appeals were overturned (UnitedHealth 99.7%). Across all MA, KFF found 53M prior-auth decisions in 2024, 7.7% denied, only 11.5% of denials appealed, and more than 8 in 10 appeals won. Denied days are unpaid receivables that never get worked, because business-office staff have no time.
solution: Read-only integration with the SNF's EHR (for example PointClickCare) plus a shared inbox for plan letters. On each denial or non-coverage notice, the system builds the clinical packet (therapy minutes, nursing notes, MDS data) mapped to Traditional Medicare coverage criteria, which MA plans must follow under the 2024 CMS rule. It drafts the reconsideration or fast-track appeal, tracks the deadlines (including the noon-the-day-before deadline for fast-track requests), and escalates to independent review. A contract RN reviews and signs. Plan-specific playbooks learn what each plan responds to.
why_now: The OIG reports came out in June 2026 and were widely covered. CMS-0057-F public reporting now shows plan-level denial and overturn data (first-of-its-kind data in August 2026: 1 in 8 standard requests denied, about two-thirds of MA appeals won). Providers can now show a board or CFO the expected value of appeals. LLM drafting makes per-appeal cost low enough to work small denials.
revenue_model: Contingency of 15-25% of recovered per-diem revenue, only on overturned denials. Optional SaaS tier for chains that want the workflow in-house.
non_obvious_insight: A 95% overturn rate with fewer than 20% of denials appealed means the constraint is clerk hours, not merits. The unworked denial pile is the largest uncollected receivable in post-acute care, and success-only pricing removes the operator's risk. Evidence: OIG results via Healthcare Dive (https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/medicare-advantage-prior-authorization-denials-hhs-oig-post-acute-care/822724/), KFF's 53M-determination analysis (https://www.kff.org/medicare/issue-brief/medicare-advantage-insurers-made-nearly-53-million-prior-authorization-determinations-in-2024/), and 2026 plan-level metrics (https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/prior-authorization-denials-vary-widely-among-insurers/827891/). Competition is real in general appeals automation, so the wedge is SNF-specific workflow plus a contingency contract, not a generic appeals tool.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 small SNF chains through state nursing-home associations. Backfill their last 6-12 months of MA denials to show a retroactive expected win rate. Sign BAAs and start filing live appeals by week 3 on a no-win-no-fee basis. Hire one part-time contract RN reviewer. Start with the two or three plans with the highest SNF denial rates and build their playbooks first.

title: Tariff Refund Recovery for Downstream Buyers
one_liner: Importers of record are collecting over $100B in tariff refunds, but the small businesses that paid tariff surcharges on their invoices are owed a share and nobody is collecting it for them.
customer: Mid-size US contractors, restaurant groups, retailers and manufacturers ($5M-$200M revenue) whose 2025-26 supplier invoices carried explicit tariff surcharges or tariff-attributed price increases.
problem: Refunds go to the importer of record, and many importers already passed the cost through. Downstream buyers may have contract or unjust-enrichment claims, but their AP teams never tracked surcharges. Small importers also find filing costly ('not without a cost,' Colorado Sun, 2026-07-02), so cash sits with parties who have no incentive to share it.
solution: Connect to QuickBooks, NetSuite or the AP inbox and extract every invoice line mentioning a tariff or surcharge. Map each vendor to its importer of record using public import records. Estimate the refund-attributable share and generate demand packets with contract citations. A partner law firm handles escalations on contingency. Default settlement is a vendor credit memo, which preserves the relationship.
why_now: More than $100B has been refunded (CNBC 2026-08-07, Forbes 2026-09-09), the government is fighting an order to refund all importers (WaPo 2026-08-11), tariff lawsuits are surging, and 25 states are challenging the replacement Section 122 tariffs. That means a second wave of surcharges to track.
revenue_model: 20-30% contingency on recovered cash or credits. After the first recovery, $299-$999 per month SaaS to track surcharges and refund clauses on future tariff swings.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone is watching who receives the refund, and nobody watches who funded it. Many invoices literally say 'tariff surcharge, pass-through.' Vendors prefer credit memos to cash, so recoveries can be quiet and relationship-safe. The same invoice-clause tooling becomes a permanent tariff-swing shield.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 SMBs through trade associations and small-business communities and pull 24 months of AP exports. Run the analysis by hand with a lawyer's template letter and produce a $1M aggregate identified-claim demo. Sign two contingent agreements and send the first ten demand letters.

title: Family Bank: Bank of Mom and Dad, Papered
one_liner: A family office's real job is governance and records, not investing; for $20/mo, give ordinary parents and adult children a promissory-note, autopay and sibling-fairness ledger for the money that already flows between them.
customer: Parents aged 55-75 who lend or give money to adult children (down-payment help, car, tuition, debt payoff, business start), sold as a pair with the adult child (28-45). Elder-law attorneys, mortgage brokers and credit unions are referral channels.
problem: Family lending is handshake-based. Zero-interest loans over $10k invite imputed-interest questions. Gifts above the $19,000 annual exclusion (2026) need Form 709 filings. Medicaid's 60-month look-back treats gifts and forgiven loans as transfers. Mortgage lenders want documented gift letters. Siblings fight at inheritance over who got what because nobody kept records. NAR's 2025 profile shows the median first-time buyer is 40 and 22% received a gift or loan from relatives or friends.
solution: A guided flow decides gift vs loan and generates a note at or above the AFR (August 2026: 4.10% short, 4.35% mid, 4.92% long). ACH autopay collects and pays, and both sides get annual interest statements. A December 'forgiveness engine' forgives up to the exclusion with proper letters. A sibling ledger records every advancement so estates can equalize. Flags fire for Form 709 and Medicaid look-back exposure, and there is a mortgage-ready gift-letter generator plus one-click export to the family's estate attorney. Attorney review is an add-on.
why_now: Median first-time buyer age hit 40 (a record), housing costs push more family help, and long-term-care costs make the Medicaid look-back a live worry for boomer parents. Instant-payment and bank-linking rails make autopay cheap. The 2026 federal estate exemption is $15M, so for most families the value is peace and records, not tax planning.
revenue_model: $20/mo per family (up to 3 active loans); $49 document packs for the free-to-paid funnel; $149 attorney review add-on with referral fees; optional servicing fee; later, a pooled family reserve product.
non_obvious_insight: The killer feature is not the loan, it is the sibling ledger. Most family money fights are about unequal treatment nobody can prove, and family offices solve this with an advancement ledger that ordinary families never get. The loan-vs-gift label is also the pivot point for tax and Medicaid consequences, so classification is the paid moment.
first_30_days: Ship a free AFR calculator and note generator aimed at 'family loan agreement' searches, and sell $49 document packs. Convert 5% to the $20/mo servicing tier. Line up 3 elder-law attorneys who receive leads and review notes. Target 50 paying families.

title: Sponsor-a-Lifeline Satellite Messaging for Missionaries
one_liner: A church-sponsored satellite messaging line plus supporter-update relay for missionaries, Bible translators and mission-aviation crews in no-coverage areas, sold to mission agencies as duty of care.
customer: Mission agencies with 50-2,000 field workers and the sending churches that sponsor individual workers.
problem: Field workers live outside coverage and agencies carry duty of care using a patchwork of individual satellite communicators. Missionaries also fund themselves through supporter updates, which stall when connectivity is bad. Churches want a tangible way to care for their people, yet direct-to-cell carriers still do not know how to price or differentiate satellite service.
solution: A neutral bundle: direct-to-cell or handheld messaging across whichever networks work (Iridium NTN, Starlink direct-to-cell, others) plus an agency dashboard with check-in cadence, geofenced security alerts and evacuation triggers. Short satellite texts are compiled into a 'prayer letter' for supporters, and a sponsor page (for example 'Sponsor Anna's lifeline at $18 per month') keeps privacy controls.
why_now: Satellite-to-phone partnerships are multiplying but 'key questions remain unresolved' on pricing and value (Satellite Today, Sept 2026). Iridium NTN Direct is expected later in 2026, and Starlink ARPU falling from $81 to $66 signals cheaper plans. Carriers and resellers need verticals with a willing payer.
revenue_model: $15-25 per field worker per month paid by the agency or sponsors, a $150-200 hardware and setup margin, and enterprise duty-of-care dashboard tiers.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer is the sending church or agency, not the traveler, and the value of connectivity is fundraising continuity as much as SOS. A 'sponsor a lifeline' framing turns safety hardware into recurring giving.
first_30_days: Approach 5 small and mid-sized agencies through a mission-agency association. Offer 20-seat pilots at $150 setup plus $18 per month per seat. Write prayer-letter templates and test the sponsor page with two sending churches.

title: Clinician-Prescribed AI Social Practice for Kids
one_liner: A bounded, transcript-visible role-play partner that speech-language pathologists prescribe to autistic and socially anxious kids, sold to districts that are legally obliged to deliver therapy minutes.
customer: School-district special-education departments, contract therapy staffing firms (SLP, psychology) and private pediatric therapy clinics.
problem: Insiders think kids plus AI is a no-go zone. Character.AI barred under-18s from open-ended chat in November 2025, and the FTC 6(b) inquiry and state laws (CA SB 243) followed. But districts must deliver IEP speech and social-communication minutes, SLP caseloads are huge and vacancies persist. Kids need many low-stakes repetitions between weekly 30-minute sessions.
solution: An anti-companion design: the SLP assigns scripted scenarios (ordering lunch, joining a game, handling teasing). There is no persona, no persistent memory and no free topics. Practice is recorded and the SLP dashboard produces the progress-monitoring data IEPs require. Parents can read transcripts. Voice-first, tuned for child speech, with no audio retention by default.
why_now: Regulators and lawsuits (Raine v. OpenAI, Pennsylvania v. Character.AI) closed the open-ended companion door, which makes scoped, clinician-in-the-loop tools the defensible lane. Speech models handle child speech far better than they did two years ago. Special-ed budgets are stretched (from memory).
revenue_model: Per-student annual licence ($150-400), much cheaper than added SLP hours at $60-100 an hour. Clinics pay per clinician seat.
non_obvious_insight: The regulated lane isn't closed, it just has a different buyer: a clinician with a legal duty to document. Designing it as the opposite of a companion (no persona, no memory, no free chat) makes it compliant by construction and defensible in the next lawsuit.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 practicing SLPs to script 30 scenarios. Build a voice prototype. Run a 4-week paid pilot with about 10 kids in one private clinic ($99 a month per child). Then approach one contract-therapy staffing firm with the pilot's progress-monitoring data.

title: Snow Mutual: Weather Swaps Between Opposite Businesses
one_liner: A peer-to-peer weather-swap exchange that nets opposite snowfall exposures inside a metro, matching per-push plow operators with seasonal-flat operators and per-push property managers so no one pays insurer-grade premiums.
customer: Independent snow-plow and landscaping contractors (10-200 trucks) and small commercial property managers, HOAs and retail owners in Great Lakes and Northeast snowbelts.
problem: Snow contracts are weather bets. A dry winter crushes per-push operators' revenue while truck notes, insurance and retainer labor stay fixed. A heavy winter blows up seasonal-flat operators' costs and property managers' per-push budgets. Traditional insurance for this is thin and expensive, so nearly everyone is unhedged.
solution: Standardized index contracts, either seasonal snowfall or count of 2+ inch events at a named NWS/airport station. They are matched inside a metro. The platform holds collateral, nets opposing positions and lays off only the residual to a reinsurer or weather-derivative desk. Onboarding asks for your contract mix and returns a 'snow exposure score' and a suggested swap. Version one is an index-linked price-collar clause in the service contract itself, which needs no insurance license. A licensed MGA structure follows.
why_now: NOAA CPC/IRI's September 2026 outlooks put a greater than 90% chance on a very strong El Niño this winter, and seasonal snowfall maps lean below normal for the Great Lakes and Northeast, with lake-effect still a wildcard. Sentiment is lopsided and uncertain. Renewals and pricing decisions happen between now and November, so contractors are actively thinking about winter risk.
revenue_model: A fee of 8-12% of matched notional, charged to both sides, plus a small annual membership. Later, a margin on the unmatched residual layer and reinsurance placement fees.
non_obvious_insight: The snow industry already contains natural hedgers on both sides of every winter. Operators with per-push books and operators with seasonal-flat books have opposite exposures, and so do property managers. The need is mostly a matching problem, and matching removes the capital cost that makes small-business weather cover uneconomic.
first_30_days: Recruit through snow-industry associations, plow-forum groups and property-management associations. Sign about 15 operators and 15 property managers in one metro. Draft the index-collar addendum with a commercial lawyer and run a pilot on winter 2026-27 contracts with small capped notionals. Line up an MGA and a reinsurance quote for the residual.

title: Half-Plate Menus for GLP-1 Diners
one_liner: A menu-engineering and POS program that turns GLP-1 diners into incremental visits through protein-first half portions.
customer: Multi-unit casual-dining and fast-casual operators with 20-300 locations.
problem: GLP-1 households cut restaurant spend about 8%, yet 48% of users say they would dine out more if smaller portions were offered.
solution: Design a 'Half-Plate' section (65-70% of full price, protein-forward, fiber-tuned), integrate it in the POS, and measure incremental visits and margin per cover.
why_now: About 12% of Americans use a GLP-1 and the oral Wegovy pill launched in January 2026 at $149-299/month, so the segment is now big enough for a dedicated menu line.
revenue_model: Per-location monthly fee plus a performance share of measured incremental visits.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders assume smaller portions cannibalize revenue, but restaurant labor and rent are per-cover costs. A visit at 70% of the check with lower food cost beats losing the visit at 100%.
first_30_days: Sign two regional chains for a 10-store test of a Half-Plate section and set up a simple visit-frequency and basket dashboard from POS exports.

title: Private Road Agreements That Save Rural Closings
one_liner: A flat-fee e-sign-and-record service that produces the road-maintenance and shared-well agreements lenders demand, then turns each road into a dues-collecting association.
customer: Listing and buyer agents and title/escrow officers in rural and mountain markets (CO, MT, ID, WA, OR, UT, NC/TN mountains, northern New England) pay $400-750 per transaction. Later, the households on each road pay $15-40 a month through the association.
problem: A house on a private road often has no enforceable maintenance agreement, only a handshake among neighbors. FHA, VA, USDA and most conventional underwriters want a recorded, legally enforceable agreement, and similar paper for shared wells, septics and driveways. The appraiser flags the private road and the problem lands on nobody. It surfaces 7-10 days before closing, the neighbors have no reason to cooperate, and the deal slips or dies. Between sales the road decays because nobody can collect dues.
solution: Software plus templated law. (1) Detect private vs public roads from county GIS and identify every benefiting parcel and owner. (2) Use state-specific agreement templates reviewed once by local counsel. (3) Run a multi-party e-sign, remote online notarization and e-recording workflow with a friendly neighbor-outreach script. (4) Add a lender-ready cover letter that answers the standard underwriting condition. (5) Upsell to a formal road association (entity, EIN, bank account, ACH dues billing, reserve tracking, lien rights where state statute allows) and shared well/septic agreements.
why_now: Affordability pushes buyers toward exurban and rural homes, and many of them rely on FHA, VA or USDA financing with strict access rules. Remote online notarization and e-recording are now legal and routine in most states. Counties are refusing to accept new roads into public maintenance. Wildfire-zone insurers and fire districts increasingly care about year-round road access and maintenance.
revenue_model: $495 flat per agreement package, paid by the seller through escrow or by a title partner, plus pass-through recording fees. $250 add-on per shared well, septic or easement agreement. Recurring: $29/month association software plus a payment fee on dues (about 3% + $3 per household per month). Referral fees from title partners.
non_obvious_insight: The road is not the deal-killer. The 4-30 neighbors who each have zero incentive to sign are. So the product is the neighbor-consent workflow, not the document. The other insider fact is that underwriters usually accept a simple recorded agreement signed by a majority of owners with proportional cost shares. You don't need a full HOA. Once a road has bank-account-backed dues, it becomes a sticky recurring customer that nobody else serves.
first_30_days: Pick 2 counties dense with private roads (for example the foothills of Larimer/Boulder CO, or Flathead MT). Pull active listings and cross-match them to county road-class GIS to find listings on private roads. Pay a local real-estate attorney about $2-3k to review one template. Cold-contact those listing agents with a specific message: your listing is on a private road, the lender will ask for this, and we deliver in 7 days. Sign 5 pilots at $495 and 2 title officers as referral partners.

title: Immunogenicity Screens for De Novo Proteins
one_liner: A fast, low-cost HLA-diverse T-cell screen and de-immunize-and-retest loop built for AI-designed proteins that have no natural template to humanize.
customer: AI protein-design startups and pharma teams with de novo miniprotein or binder programs approaching IND, and design-tool vendors who want immunogenicity data as proof of quality.
problem: Trend chain: AI binder design is cheap and abundant. Designs are entering the clinic (a de novo PD-L1 miniprotein has reached first-in-human imaging). But de novo proteins have no germline or humanization playbook, in silico epitope predictors over-call risk, and ex vivo T-cell panels are custom studies at CROs. PBMC vials cost about $460 each, so early-stage designers skip the test until a late failure.
solution: Bulk-buy an HLA-typed donor PBMC bank (30-50 donors covering major alleles). Run 96-well T-cell activation and proliferation assays plus MHC-associated peptide analysis on batches of 20-100 candidates per week. Return per-sequence hotspot maps, feed AI deimmunization redesign, then retest. Publish calibration against known immunogenic and non-immunogenic clinical proteins.
why_now: AI-drug funding tops $6B in 2026, and frontier-lab designs hit about 27% in Adaptyv's blind test, so many de novo programs are heading toward IND. FDA's shift toward human-relevant in vitro methods favors ex vivo immunogenicity assays.
revenue_model: $2-5k per candidate at batch scale, $50-150k for full deimmunization campaigns, and platform subscriptions for design companies.
non_obvious_insight: The cost driver is donors, not reagents. Buying donor lots at scale and running big plate batches flips the economics from 'per-molecule custom study' to 'per plate'. Every screen also calibrates the predictors that AI designers will later pay for, which builds a data flywheel.
first_30_days: Contract an existing immunology lab staffed by ex-CRO scientists. Order 30 HLA-typed PBMC lots at bulk pricing. Test 10 published de novo binders and 5 clinical reference proteins. Publish a preprint and pitch 10 protein-design startups.
